title: Decision Intelligence Systems

meta_description: Decision Intelligence Systems from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: A practical build of Decision Intelligence Systems: two weeks to a signed baseline, six to a working pilot, twelve to an industrialized deployment with the delta reported against week zero.

High-volume decisions — credit, claims, pricing, triage, fraud, service routing — deserve dedicated decision infrastructure, not rules buried in application code. We build decision hubs that combine predictive models, business rules and agentic reasoning behind one decision API, with champion-challenger testing, decision policies as versioned artifacts, and full replay so every outcome can be explained months later to an auditor or a customer.

The design principle is separability: models score, policy decides, and humans supervise. That separation lets risk teams change policy without retraining models, lets data scientists ship models without touching code paths, and gives compliance a single place to inspect what decision logic actually ran on any given day.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
